what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to authorize town counsel to send a response to an Open Meeting Law complaint about the November 9 meeting, copied to the Attorney General.
The complainant said the response did not address her question about no agenda item being posted for the board's votes on warrant articles, and that she may go to the Attorney General.
The town manager reported that the cleaning contract for town buildings expired and preliminary estimates run above the budgeted amount, which a special Town Meeting would be asked to cover.
The board discussed converting streetlights to LED, which would need a utility request for purchase cost and a bid, possibly funded by competitive Green Communities money.
The board reappointed a member to the architectural preservation district committee and approved three 2018 licenses.

why_it_matters: A higher cleaning contract cost would reach residents through a special Town Meeting appropriation, a vote they could be asked to take, paid mostly from taxes.

The Open Meeting Law dispute concerns whether the public was told in advance, through the posted agenda, that the board would vote on warrant articles, so it bears on how Town Meeting items are noticed.
LED streetlight conversion could change what the town pays for street lighting, depending on purchase cost and grant funding.
watch_next: A possible complaint to the Attorney General over the Open Meeting Law response, as the complainant said she may file.
A special Town Meeting article to appropriate the added cleaning contract cost.
